etymologies.etymologyHTML: From stick +‎ -y.

definitions.definition: Tending to stick; able to adhere via the drying of a viscous substance.

quote.citation: 2016 June 5, Thomas Manch, “CuriousCity: What happens to my library books when I return them?”, in Stuff‎[1], archived from the original on 2019-05-04:
quote.text: Particularly sticky books are cleaned with methylated spirits.

quote.citation: 1989 December 24, Abe Rybeck, “Liberation Without Permission, Pleasure Without Apology”, in Gay Community News, volume 17, number 24, page 5:
quote.text: GCN is not just another clipboard of polite press releases. GCN is the sticky questions, the sweet moments, and the dirty stories that make up our lives.

quote.citation: 2020 June 25, Tegan Bennett Daylight, “My mother taught me the joy of reading. I remember her through books”, in Katharine Viner, editor, The Guardian‎[2], London: Guardian News & Media, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 2023-05-27:
quote.text: Among the books Mum brought me to read when I was a child were The Secret Garden and A Little Princess, as well as their author Frances Hodgson Burnett's smash hit, Little Lord Fauntleroy. I haven't met an adult my age who has read this book but I did so several times. It's a sticky book, guided by that strange Victorian obsession with "the little mother" – the same obsession that Virginia Woolf, a child of Victorian parents, grappled with in her diaries and her fiction. Somehow, though, I learned to overlook the archaic, to be open to the oddnesses of different eras, and to read for something else.

quote.citation: 2014 September 8, Michael White, “Roll up, roll up! The Amazing Salmond will show a Scotland you won't believe”, in Alan Rusbridger, editor, The Guardian‎[3], London: Guardian News & Media, →ISSN, →OCLC, archived from the original on 2022-10-13:
quote.text: Salmond studied medieval Scottish history as well as economics at university so he cannot say he has not had fair warning – it was even more turbulent and bloody than England at that time – and plenty of Scotland's kings and leaders came to a sticky end. If it happens this time, it won't be dull.

definitions.definition: Of weather: hot and windless and with high humidity, so that people feel sticky from sweating.

quote.citation: 2008, Robert K. Fitts, Wally Yonamine: The Man Who Changed Japanese Baseball:
quote.text: The baby was due in December and the hot, sticky August weather was making Jane uncomfortable.

quote.citation: 1981 December 27, “Robert Bobbie Bob, Inc (personal advertisement)”, in Gay Community News, volume 9, number 23, page 18:
quote.text: Love you and miss you and wish you all the sticky things one wishes at this season for someone one loves.

definitions.definition: (finance) Tending to stay the same; resistant to change.
(computing, of a window) Appearing on all virtual desktops.
(Internet, of threads on a bulletin board) Fixed at the top of the list of topics or threads so as to keep it in view.
(Internet, of a website) Compelling enough to keep visitors from leaving.

A woman has come to me with the complain: 70% of the visits last 30 seconds or less.

definitions.definition: (informal) Resembling or characteristic of a stick.
A sticky note, such as a post-it note.
(Internet) A discussion thread fixed at the top of the list of topics or threads so as to keep it in view.
(manufacturing) A small adhesive particle found in wastepaper.
(slang) Sticky-icky; marijuana, especially the sticky, resin-covered buds.

quote.citation: 2006, Noire [pseudonym], Thug-A-Licious: An Urban Erotic Tale, New York, N.Y.: One World, Ballantine Books, →ISBN, page 268:
quote.text: We'd smoked some nice sticky that night and fucked with some Erk and Jerk too, so my head was still cloudy when Pimp came in the room and said get up.
Still smoking sticky, it ain't no other option / Not for made niggas, and I'm never stopping

quote.citation: 2014, Jagada Chambers, Based on a True Story:
quote.text: As drunk as I was, all I could think about was getting some sticky down my lungs.

definitions.definition: (Internet, bulletin boards, transitive) to fix a thread at the top of the list of topics or threads so as to keep it in view.
